note: Hostile vectors for the R75 / R100.A2 gate. Every banned literal lives HERE, as JSON data, because .json is not an executable extension in .github/r75-policy.json scan.includeExtensions — so the regression suite can exercise real banned tokens without the suite itself becoming an R75 violation. This is a fixture-DATA exclusion only: the executable spec that reads this file (test/ci/r75-gate.spec.ts) IS scanned, as is every other test source.

legacyAlgorithm.note: The deleted pre-repair CI shell implementation, reproduced so each regression case can prove it is sensitive to the exact defect being repaired (negative control). literalTokens are counted with grep -cF semantics (matching LINES, not occurrences); counts are summed across ALL tokens into one aggregate net; any line matching exemptLinePattern is discarded whole; excludeSuffixes drop test and spec sources entirely.

cases.name: same-token net-zero: an existing banned cast is only relocated
cases.why: R75 bans net ADDITIONS. A pure move of the same token is net zero and must pass, or the gate blocks harmless refactors.

cases.name: cross-token substitution: delete one banned token, introduce a different one
cases.why: The exact loophole R75 exists to close (as never +119%, as unknown as +68%). Aggregate cross-token netting let a deletion pay for an introduction.

cases.name: multiple occurrences on a single line

src/a.ts: const b = (y as any) + (z as any) + (w as any);

cases.why: grep -c counts matching LINES. Three introduced casts were reported as one, so two of them were free.

cases.name: changed test and co-located spec sources are scanned

test/ci/thing.spec.ts: const t = v as unknown as string;
src/top.spec.ts: const s = v as unknown as string;
src/nested/deep.test.ts: const d = v as unknown as string;

cases.why: R131 records R75 being misread as src-only. The old spec/test excludes left every changed test file unscanned, and R75 bans these tokens in test/ as well as src/.

cases.name: top-level source file is scanned
cases.why: Top-level files must not fall through the scan the way a bare src/**/*.ts pathspec drops them.

cases.name: documented suppression sharing a line with another banned token

src/a.ts: // @ts-expect-error upstream typings are wrong (see ticket #4821) -- const q = r as any;

cases.why: The suppression exception must affect only that directive. Discarding the whole line hid every other violation on it.

cases.name: suppression with a non-empty reason and nothing else is permitted

src/a.ts: // @ts-expect-error legacy SDK returns a loose shape here

cases.why: R75 permits @ts-expect-error <reason> with a non-empty same-line reason. No issue-number requirement exists in canon; the old EXEMPT_RE invented one and failed every compliant suppression.

cases.name: suppression with no reason is a violation
cases.why: A bare suppression is the @ts-ignore loophole under a different name.

cases.name: suppression whose reason is only punctuation is a violation
cases.why: Bounded reason validation: non-empty means substance, not a dash. It is deliberately not an issue-tracker lookup or a language classifier.

cases.name: every spelling of the swallowed-error catch is detected
cases.why: 50-failures #36. The old split of three no-space literals plus a parametrized regex matched NEITHER '.catch(() => null)' NOR '.catch(() => {})' — the forms Prettier actually produces — so the canonical R75 literals were undetectable in formatted source.

cases.name: declaration files, vendored trees and generated bundles stay excluded

src/types/global.d.ts: declare const loose: unknown; // as any

cases.why: Exclusions must stay narrow: declarations, vendored and generated output, and non-executable extensions only.

cases.name: clean pass on a real change with no banned tokens
cases.why: The gate must not fire on compliant work.

cases.name: renamed path carrying an existing banned token is net zero
cases.why: Rename detection must not read a moved pre-existing violation as a new introduction.

cases.name: deleting a path that carried banned tokens is net negative
cases.why: Removing violations must never be penalised.

cases.name: staged mode measures the index, not unstaged working bytes
cases.why: The hook gates what is about to be committed. A violation still in the working tree is not yet a commit.

cases.name: staged mode fails once the violation is staged
cases.why: Hook and CI must agree on the same content.

operationalCases.name: unresolvable base fails loudly instead of scanning an empty diff
missing base is not an empty diff
empty base string is not an empty diff
